_doc: Towns PROPOSED for the target set but not yet adopted. Deliberately kept OUT of ../zips.json, because zips.json is the scrape config -- anything listed there gets hydrated on the next run. A town lands here first, gets a tier in tierlist.html, and only then is it promoted into zips.json and scraped. That is the gate: no tier, no hydration.
_promote: When a candidate earns a tier, move its entry into ../zips.json (name/county/zips/dist_mi) and delete it here. Check the `note` field first -- several of these overlap towns already tracked and would double-count a ZIP.

candidates.name: Hanover Township
candidates.note: OVERLAP: 07927 is Cedar Knolls, already tracked and tiered B. Hanover Twp contains it. Promoting both double-counts that ZIP -- decide which entry owns 07927 first.

candidates.name: Mendham Township
candidates.note: OVERLAP: shares postal ZIP 07945 with Mendham (Borough), already tracked and tiered B. They are two separate municipalities on one ZIP -- a ZIP-keyed scrape cannot tell them apart.

candidates.name: Pompton Plains
candidates.note: Not a municipality -- a section of Pequannock Township (which is not tracked). Same shape as Cedar Knolls/Towaco in the existing set, so it works, but its tax and school figures resolve to Pequannock.

candidates.name: North Haledon
candidates.note: OVERLAP: 07508 covers BOTH North Haledon and Haledon; Haledon has no separate ZIP. Promoting both double-counts 07508.

candidates.name: Haledon
candidates.note: OVERLAP: shares ZIP 07508 with North Haledon -- see above. A ZIP-keyed scrape returns one pool of sales for both towns.
